# Motion.page SDK — Architecture & Internals

## Package Overview

```
@motion.page/sdk
├── version: 0.1.1
├── type: "module"
├── sideEffects: true          ← tree shaking is intentionally disabled
├── peerDependencies: {}       ← zero runtime dependencies
└── dist/
    ├── index.js               ← ESM build
    ├── index.cjs              ← CommonJS build
    ├── index.d.ts             ← TypeScript declarations
    └── motion-sdk.browser.js  ← IIFE browser build
```

**Zero runtime dependencies** — everything (animation engine, easing functions, color parsing, SVG utilities, text splitting) is implemented from scratch. No GSAP, no Anime.js, no dependencies at all.

---

## Build Outputs

| File | Format | Usage |
|------|--------|-------|
| `dist/index.js` | ESM | `import { Motion } from '@motion.page/sdk'` |
| `dist/index.cjs` | CJS | `require('@motion.page/sdk')` |
| `dist/index.d.ts` | Types | TypeScript declarations |
| `dist/motion-sdk.browser.js` | IIFE | `<script src="...">` — exposes `window.Motion`, `window.MotionTimeline` |

The package ships **pre-built**. Consumers do not need special bundler configuration. Works with Vite, webpack, Rollup, esbuild, and direct `<script>` tags.

**Build command:**
```bash
tsc -p tsconfig.build.json && bun build src/index.ts --outdir dist --minify
```

---

## Architecture

### Registry Pattern

The SDK is organized around two registries:

**Engine registry** (`Engine.ts`)
- Singleton engine instance
- Stores all named `Timeline` instances by name
- Coordinates the animation frame loop (RAF)
- Provides `getTimeline(name)`, `killAll()`, `killAnimationsForTargets()`

**SDKRegistry** (`registries/SDKRegistry.ts`)
- A plain object dictionary where modules self-register on import
- Used by the trigger system and utility modules to register their constructors
- Avoids circular imports between modules

### Trigger Self-Registration (Side-Effect Imports)

Each trigger and utility module **registers itself** with the SDK when imported. This is why `sideEffects: true` is set in `package.json` — tree shaking would remove these registrations.

From `src/index.ts`:
```ts
// Each import triggers self-registration via SDKRegistry
import './triggers/EventTrigger';
import './triggers/ScrollTrigger';
import './triggers/PageLoadTrigger';
import './triggers/MouseMoveTrigger';
import './triggers/GestureTrigger';
import './triggers/CursorTrigger';
import './triggers/PageExitTrigger';

import './utils/ColorParser';
import './utils/FilterParser';
import './utils/DrawSVGParser';
import './utils/TextSplitter';
import './utils/StyleReset';
import './stagger/StaggerResolver';
import './fit/FitResolver';
```

This pattern enables extensibility: a new trigger type just needs to call `TriggerManager.registerTrigger('name', TriggerClass)` and import its file.

### Module Hierarchy

```
src/index.ts                    ← Public entry point
├── core/Motion.ts              ← Motion() function + static methods
├── core/Timeline.ts            ← Timeline class (playback, triggers, each-mode)
├── core/Engine.ts              ← Singleton animation engine, RAF loop, registry
├── core/Animation.ts           ← Single animation instance (from/to/duration)
├── core/AnimationBuilder.ts    ← Builds Animation from AnimationConfig
├── registries/
│   ├── SDKRegistry.ts          ← Module self-registration dictionary
│   └── EasingRegistry.ts       ← Easing function registry
├── triggers/
│   ├── TriggerManager.ts       ← Coordinates all trigger types
│   ├── EventTrigger.ts         ← Hover + Click triggers (self-registers)
│   ├── ScrollTrigger.ts        ← ScrollTrigger (self-registers)
│   ├── PageLoadTrigger.ts      ← DOMContentLoaded trigger (self-registers)
│   ├── MouseMoveTrigger.ts     ← Mouse position trigger (self-registers)
│   ├── GestureTrigger.ts       ← Gesture input trigger (self-registers)
│   ├── CursorTrigger.ts        ← Custom cursor (self-registers)
│   └── PageExitTrigger.ts      ← Link click intercept (self-registers)
├── render/
│   └── TransformCache.ts       ← Per-element transform compositing cache
├── utils/
│   ├── ColorParser.ts          ← CSS color string → r,g,b,a + interpolation
│   ├── FilterParser.ts         ← CSS filter → individual properties
│   ├── DrawSVGParser.ts        ← drawSVG string/object → stroke-dashoffset
│   ├── TextSplitter.ts         ← Split text into char/word/line spans
│   ├── StyleReset.ts           ← Inline style tracking + restoration
│   ├── PositionParser.ts       ← Timeline position string parser
│   ├── PropertyParser.ts       ← CSS property type detection + value reading
│   ├── TargetResolver.ts       ← TargetInput → Element[] / object[]
│   └── MotionUtils.ts          ← Public utility functions
├── stagger/
│   └── StaggerResolver.ts      ← Stagger delay computation
├── fit/
│   └── FitResolver.ts          ← FLIP-style bounding rect measurement
└── types/
    ├── index.ts                ← Internal types barrel
    └── public.ts               ← Public types re-exported as Types.*
```

---

## Core Subsystems

### `from` / `to` Resolution (`core/AnimationBuilder.ts`)

When `AnimationBuilder` processes an `AnimationConfig`, it resolves the missing endpoint before handing off to the animation engine:

**Computed style reads (at build time)**

If `from` is provided but `to` is omitted (or vice versa), `AnimationBuilder` reads the element's **current computed CSS** via `PropertyParser.ts` (`getComputedStyle` for CSS properties, `TransformCache` for transform properties) to fill in the missing endpoint.

This read happens **once at build time** (when the `Timeline` is first constructed), not per-frame. If the element's CSS changes after build, the resolved endpoint stays fixed.

**Transform reads via TransformCache**

For transform properties (`x`, `y`, `scale`, etc.) the computed value is not directly available from `getComputedStyle` (which returns a matrix). `TransformCache` maintains a per-element cache of the current SDK-managed transform values. If an element has never been animated, all transforms default to their natural values (`x: 0`, `y: 0`, `scale: 1`, etc.).

**`from`-only swap (the "from tween" behavior)**

When only `from` is specified:
1. The SDK reads current CSS as `to`
2. The animation is constructed as a `fromTo` tween: element jumps to `from` values at `progress=0`, interpolates to the resolved `to` values at `progress=1`
3. On `reverse()`, the element animates back to the `from` values
4. On `kill()`, the `from` values are **not** left on the element — `StyleReset` restores the original pre-animation CSS

**`to`-only behavior**

When only `to` is specified:
1. The SDK reads current CSS as the starting point (implicit `from`)
2. The animation is constructed as a standard `to` tween: element animates from its current state to the `to` values
3. On `kill()`, `StyleReset` restores the original CSS

**Practical implication**: Because the resolved endpoint is read at build time, `Motion.set()` before constructing a timeline will change what gets resolved as the "current CSS". This is the correct pattern for pre-positioning elements before an entrance animation.

---

### Transform Cache (`render/TransformCache.ts`)

CSS transforms (`x`, `y`, `rotate`, `scale`, etc.) cannot be applied independently via `element.style.transform` without overwriting each other. The SDK maintains a **per-element transform cache** that composites all active transform properties into a single `transform` string.

When `x: 100` and `rotate: 45` are animated simultaneously on the same element, the cache merges them: `translateX(100px) rotate(45deg)`.

On `kill()` and `Motion.reset()`, the cache is cleared and the original inline transform is restored (if any existed before the SDK took over).

### CSS Transition Handling

CSS `transition` properties on animated elements would fight the SDK's frame-by-frame rendering. The SDK automatically:

1. **Saves** each element's current `transition` value at animation build time
2. **Disables** transitions (`transition: none !important`) when the timeline starts playing
3. **Restores** the original transition value when the timeline completes or is killed

This is transparent to users — CSS transitions just work alongside SDK animations.

### `will-change` Optimization

For elements with transform animations (`x`, `y`, `scale`, `rotate`, etc.), the SDK automatically applies `will-change: transform` to hint the browser to promote the element to its own compositor layer. This is cleaned up on `kill()` and `clear()`.

### StyleReset (`utils/StyleReset.ts`)

Tracks all inline styles applied by the SDK to each element. On `kill()` or `reset()`:
- Animation-applied inline styles are removed
- If the element had no inline style before the SDK ran, the `style` attribute is removed entirely
- If the element had existing inline styles, only SDK-applied properties are removed

### Text Splitter (`utils/TextSplitter.ts`)

Splits text content into `<span>` elements for per-character/word/line animation.

**Key behaviors:**
- **Preserves inline element structure**: `<span class="accent">word</span>` wrappers survive splitting. Only bare text nodes are replaced.
- **Adds data attributes** for CSS targeting: `data-split-char`, `data-split-word`, `data-split-line` with corresponding index attributes.
- **Marks root element** with `[data-split]` attribute.
- **`mask: true`** wraps each split element in an `overflow: hidden` parent (`[data-split-mask]`).
- **Reversion**: `Motion.reset(target)` or `tl.kill()` reverts the DOM to original text content.

### Each-Mode (`Timeline.ts`)

When `each: true` is set on a trigger, the `Timeline` clones itself once per matched element, creating independent per-element timeline instances. These are stored in `_eachInstances` on the parent timeline.

- `playNext` / `playPrevious` gesture actions cycle through `_eachInstances` (only available in each-mode).
- Each instance shares the same animation shape but has its own playback state.
- Killing the parent timeline kills all each-instances.

### Position Parser (`utils/PositionParser.ts`)

Parses position strings for timeline entries and `tl.call()`:

| Input | Resolution |
|-------|-----------|
| `number` | Absolute time in seconds |
| `"+=N"` | `previousEnd + N` |
| `"-=N"` | `previousEnd - N` |
| `"<"` | `previousStart` |
| `">"` | `previousEnd` |
| `"<N"` | `previousStart + N` |
| `">-N"` | `previousEnd - N` |

Supports seconds (`1.5`), milliseconds-as-floats, and percentage-of-viewport strings for scroll `end` values.

### DrawSVG Parser (`utils/DrawSVGParser.ts`)

Converts `drawSVG` values to `stroke-dashoffset`/`stroke-dasharray` changes. Auto-computes total path length via `getTotalLength()` if `stroke-dasharray` is not set.

**Supported input formats:**
- `"0% 100%"` — percentage pair (start end)
- `"50%"` — shorthand for `"0% 50%"`
- `"100px 500px"` — pixel range
- `"true"` — full stroke
- `"false"` / `"none"` — hidden
- `{ start: 0, end: 100 }` — object with **percentage** values 0–100

### Color Parser (`utils/ColorParser.ts`)

Parses CSS color strings to RGBA components for interpolation. Supports: named colors, hex (`#rgb`, `#rgba`, `#rrggbb`, `#rrggbbaa`), `rgb()`, `rgba()`, `hsl()`, `hsla()`.

### Filter Parser (`utils/FilterParser.ts`)

Parses CSS filter strings (`blur()`, `brightness()`, `contrast()`, `saturate()`, `hue-rotate()`, `drop-shadow()`) into individual animatable components, enabling smooth interpolation between filter states.

---

## Trigger System Details

### PageLoadTrigger

`onPageLoad()` registers the timeline with the `PageLoadTrigger` singleton. On `DOMContentLoaded`:

1. All registered timelines are sorted by their `timing` config (`'before'`, `'during'`, `'after'`)
2. Played in order

**If `DOMContentLoaded` has already fired** (common in SPAs, `<script>` at bottom of body, or framework `onMount()` callbacks), the timeline plays **immediately** on registration without waiting.

### ScrollTrigger

Uses `IntersectionObserver` for performant scroll detection plus `requestAnimationFrame` for scrub smoothing. Manages:
- Spacer elements (`[data-scrolltrigger-spacer]`) for pinned sections
- Debug marker elements (`[data-scrolltrigger-markers]`)
- `Motion.cleanup()` removes these DOM artifacts

Auto-refreshes on `window.resize` with a 200ms debounce.

### GestureTrigger

Listens for `pointermove`, `touchmove`, `wheel`, and `scroll` events. Uses unified delta tracking across all input types.

**`stopDelay`** uses `setTimeout` to detect inactivity. Note: value is in **milliseconds**, unlike most other time values in the SDK which use seconds.

**`lockAxis`**: Once movement begins, the dominant axis (whichever has larger delta) is locked for the gesture session. Prevents diagonal drift on swipe interactions.

**`preventDefault: true`**: Makes touch/wheel event listeners non-passive. Can impact browser scroll performance — only use when you need to completely override native scrolling.

### CursorTrigger

Replaces native cursor with a DOM element that follows the mouse. Maintains three states: `default`, `hover`, `click`. The `hover` state activates when the cursor moves over elements matching `hover.targets`.

**`type: 'text'`**: Reads `mp-cursor-text` or `mp-cursor-tooltip` from hovered elements, renders text into cursor. Uses `text` config for CSS on the text node.

**`type: 'media'`**: Reads `mp-cursor-media` URLs from hovered elements. Supports images and `.mp4`/`.webm` video. Blocks `file://` and `data:` URLs as a security measure.

## Browser Globals (IIFE Build)

```js
window.Motion        // The Motion() function + static methods
window.MotionTimeline // The Timeline class (for creating anonymous timelines)
```

`MotionTimeline` use case:
```js
const tl = new MotionTimeline();
// Creates an anonymous (unnamed) timeline not registered in the engine
```

---

## No Tree Shaking

`"sideEffects": true` in `package.json` tells bundlers that **all files in this package have side effects** and must not be removed during tree shaking.

This is intentional: the trigger modules (`EventTrigger.ts`, `ScrollTrigger.ts`, etc.) and utility modules register themselves into `SDKRegistry` when their module code runs. If bundlers eliminated these imports as "unused", the self-registration calls would never execute and the corresponding features would silently not work.

Consequence: the entire SDK bundle is always included when you import `@motion.page/sdk`, regardless of which features you use. The minified bundle size is what you pay.
